canonical_attachment_policy: One duplicated chapter witness; attach each atomic claim to its matching verse row. Attach the chapter introduction to verse 1. Never count duplicate rows as independent witnesses.

claims.voice_position: Ibn Kathir statement with reported alternative
claims.statement_en: The chapter is described as Medinan, while a Meccan classification is also reported.

claims.voice_position: Anas ibn Malik / Prophetic report transmitted through Ahmad and Muslim routes
claims.statement_en: A report presents the surah as newly revealed during a brief doze and explains al-Kawthar as a river granted in Paradise, associated with abundant good and a pool visited by the community.
claims.evidence_anchor_ar: هو نهر أعطانيه ربي عز وجل في الجنة عليه خير كثير ... هو حوض ترد عليه أمتي

claims.voice_position: Ibn Kathir / legal and recitational inferences reported
claims.statement_en: He notes that many readers infer a Medinan setting from the report and that many jurists infer that the basmala belongs to and was revealed with the surah.
claims.evidence_anchor_ar: استدل به كثير من القراء ... وكثير من الفقهاء على أن البسملة من السورة

claims.voice_position: Ibn Abbas through Sa'id ibn Jubayr
claims.statement_en: Ibn Abbas explains al-Kawthar as the abundant good God granted the Prophet, with the river in Paradise included within that broader good.
claims.evidence_anchor_ar: عن سعيد بن جبير عن ابن عباس ... هو الخير الذي أعطاه الله إياه ... النهر الذي في الجنة من الخير الذي أعطاه الله إياه ... الكوثر الخير الكثير
claims.translation_state: core interpretation aligned in abridged English; printed Arabic routes are abridged
claims.evidence_state: arabic route and bounded English context verified

claims.statement_en: Mujahid explains al-Kawthar as abundant good in this world and the hereafter.
claims.evidence_anchor_ar: حتى قال مجاهد هو الخير الكثير في الدنيا والآخرة
claims.translation_state: controlled research translation from Arabic; corresponding live English sentence absent
claims.evidence_state: Arabic attribution verified; chain absent in checked excerpt

claims.evidence_state: Arabic attribution verified; chain absent in checked excerpt

claims.evidence_state: Arabic attribution verified; chain absent in checked excerpt

claims.statement_en: The command is connected with prayer to the Lord and the slaughter of sacrificial camels.

claims.voice_position: Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, Said ibn Jubayr, and Qatada report
claims.statement_en: A named report cluster identifies the hostile referent as al-As ibn Wa'il.
claims.evidence_anchor_ar: قال ابن عباس ومجاهد وسعيد بن جبير وقتادة نزلت في العاص بن وائل

claims.statement_en: The hater of Muhammad and of the guidance he brought is called the lesser, humiliated one whose remembrance is cut off.
claims.evidence_anchor_ar: إن مبغضك ... هو الأبتر الأقل الأذل المنقطع ذكره

claims.statement_en: A competing occasion report identifies the hostile referent as Uqba ibn Abi Mu'ayt.
claims.evidence_anchor_ar: وقال شمر بن عطية نزلت في عقبة بن أبي معيط

claims.voice_position: Ibn Abbas and Ikrima report; al-Bazzar route retained separately
claims.statement_en: Another competing report identifies Ka'b ibn al-Ashraf and a group of Quraysh; the accompanying route through Ikrima reports Ka'b's favorable answer to Quraysh against Muhammad.
claims.evidence_anchor_ar: وقال ابن عباس أيضا وعكرمة نزلت في كعب بن الأشرف وجماعة من كفار قريش

claims.voice_position: Ata report and separate Ibn Abbas report
claims.statement_en: Further alternatives identify Abu Lahab in connection with the death of Muhammad's son, or Abu Jahl.
claims.evidence_anchor_ar: وعن عطاء نزلت في أبي لهب ... وعن ابن عباس نزلت في أبي جهل

claims.statement_en: After preserving the named occasion reports, Ibn Kathir generalizes the verse to every person characterized by hostility toward Muhammad and his message.
claims.evidence_anchor_ar: وهذا يعم جميع من اتصف بذلك ممن ذكر وغيرهم

translation_review.finding: The abridged English block covers the core prayer/sacrifice, al-As, enemy, and cut-off meanings. English coverage has not been established for the separately retained Uqba, Ka'b/Quraysh, Abu Lahab, Abu Jahl, and universalizing details; these remain Arabic-source claims, not silently translated claims.
